records.text: On 2023-05-22, the user supplied information about defects liability periods (DLPs) in Australian building contracts. The supplied material said a DLP helps principals accept practical completion despite minor defects or punch-list items, incentivises contractors to meet required standards, and avoids the interface risks and extra costs of hiring an unfamiliar third party to rectify defects. It also said contractors may receive final milestone payments or progress claims without waiting for minor defects to be fixed, and can preserve the integrity of fitness-for-purpose or design-life warranties by doing rectification themselves.

On 2023-05-22, the user supplied material stating that expiry of a defects liability period does not necessarily end a construction contractor’s obligations or prevent a principal from seeking common-law damages for defects. The material said limitation periods depend on whether the contract is a deed or an agreement and on applicable state legislation: up to 12 years for a deed and up to 6 years for an agreement. It also said damages are the usual common-law remedy, while specific performance requiring rectification may be unavailable except in exceptional circumstances; a contractual DLP gives the principal a period to require rectification and the contractor an opportunity to perform it.

records.text: In Wiremu Grace’s story “How Māui Brought Fire to the World,” curious Māui extinguishes every fire in the world to discover where fire comes from. When the frightened villagers ask their rangatira Taranga for help, Māui volunteers to visit the fire goddess Mahuika, his ancestress. Mahuika welcomes him as her grandchild and gives him a fingernail of fire. Māui repeatedly extinguishes the fire and returns with excuses to obtain more fingernails and then toenails. When Mahuika realizes he has tricked her, she throws a burning toenail at him. Māui transforms into a hawk, but the fire singes the undersides of his wings red. He calls on his ancestor Tāwhirimātea, who sends rain to quench the fires. Mahuika’s last toenail of fire lands in several trees, including the Kaikōmako. Māui returns to the village with dry Kaikōmako wood and teaches the villagers to make fire by rubbing sticks together. The story explains the hawk’s red feathers and the origin of fire-making from wood.
records.topic: Māori legend of the origin of fire

records.text: The assistant’s narrative outline for “How Māui Brought Fire to the World” identified the settings as a village and Mahuika’s scorching mountain; the main characters as Māui, Taranga, Mahuika, and the villagers; and the plot as Māui extinguishing the fires, obtaining fire from Mahuika through repeated deception, escaping her flames as a hawk, and receiving rain from Tāwhirimātea. The outline identified curiosity, trickery, ancestry, and nature as themes. Its plot summary omitted the story’s conclusion that Māui teaches the villagers to make fire by rubbing dry Kaikōmako sticks together.

In Facets, a CI Integration is a central repository for managing a service’s Docker images. It can be environment-type or release-stream-type, with a separate bucket for each environment or release stream. Images can be added by pushing them with Facets CLI (facetctl), which can integrate with CodeBuild, Jenkins, CircleCI, or GitHub Actions, or by promoting builds through a promotion workflow. Promotion workflows are also environment-type or release-stream-type and attach to a CI Integration of the matching type; they define controlled build-promotion paths and retain audit information about who promoted which build and when.

The current Artifact CI / CI Integration page makes it tedious and time-consuming to attach promotion workflows because users must edit each Artifact CI individually. The dominant use case—estimated at 90%—is attaching one promotion workflow to multiple Artifact CIs. The page name may also fail to communicate its purpose and confuse users.
